title: Cartesian monoidal straightening of a cocartesian fibration
statement:
Use the infinity categories, spaces and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], with a larger universe for categories of categories. Let $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be a cocartesian fibration of infinity categories: every arrow $f:b\to b'$ and $e\in\mathcal E_b$ admits a lift $e\to f_!e$ over $f$ such that, for every $z\in\mathcal E$, the square of mapping spaces induced by this lift and by $p$ is a homotopy pullback. Write $\Phi:\mathcal B\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ for its classifying functor, with $\Phi(b)=\mathcal E_b$ and $\Phi(f)=f_!$. Products here are characterized by product mapping spaces and terminal objects by contractible mapping spaces into them. Assume $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal B$ have finite products, $p$ preserves them, and a product of $p$-cocartesian arrows is again $p$-cocartesian. Then $\Phi$ has a canonical lax symmetric monoidal structure for cartesian products. Its finite-arity structure functor is
$$\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal E_{b_i}\longrightarrow\mathcal E_{\prod_{i\in I}b_i},\qquad(e_i)\longmapsto\prod_{i\in I}e_i;$$
for $I=\varnothing$ this selects $1_{\mathcal E}\in\mathcal E_{1_{\mathcal B}}$. Here a symmetric monoidal infinity category means a cocartesian fibration over the nerve of finite pointed sets whose fiber over $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$ is the $n$-fold power of its fiber over $\langle1\rangle$ via the inert projections, and lax symmetric monoidal means a functor over that nerve preserving cocartesian arrows above inert maps (those with singleton inverse images at every non-basepoint). Cartesian monoidal structures use finite products as their operations. Thus the asserted structure includes coherent compatibility with permutations, partitions into blocks, nullary operations and all higher simplices, not only binary comparison functors.

source.place: Ramzi, A monoidal Grothendieck construction for infinity-categories, Definition 1.11, Theorem 2.1 and Remark 2.2, specialized to cartesian monoidal structures.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope] to $\mathcal E,\mathcal B$ and the finite-product-preserving $p$. This gives actual infinity categories and a functor $q=p^{\times}:\mathcal E^{\times}\to\mathcal B^{\times}$ over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$, with $q$ acting coordinatewise on tuple fibers. In particular its fiber over $b=(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$ is $\prod_i\mathcal E_{b_i}$. This assertion includes $n=0$, where the fiber is terminal. We now prove that $q$ itself is a cocartesian fibration, rather than assuming a monoidal straightening theorem.

source.place: Construction 2.4.1.4, Proposition 2.4.1.5, Corollary 2.4.1.9; Ramzi Theorem 2.1, tuple-fiber construction.

proof.text: Write a base arrow $a:b\to b'$ over $\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$ as its component maps $f_j:\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}b_i\to b'_j$, using [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. For $e=(e_i)$ over $b$, put $v_j=\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}e_i$. Finite-product preservation identifies $p(v_j)$ with the source of $f_j$. Choose a $p$-cocartesian lift $u_j:v_j\to e'_j$ of $f_j$, which exists by the hypothesis on $p$. These maps represent an arrow $u:e\to e'$ of $\mathcal E^{\times}$ over $a$. Empty blocks use $v_j=1_{\mathcal E}$ and $p(1_{\mathcal E})\simeq1_{\mathcal B}$; no nonempty-block hypothesis is used.

source.place: Theorem 2.1 construction and Definition 1.11; explicit blockwise lifts for cartesian products.

proof.text:
Check the intrinsic cocartesian square for $u$. Fix any test tuple $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ and a pointed map $\beta:\langle m\rangle\to\langle r\rangle$. The mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope] identifies the component over $\beta$ of that square with the product, over $k=1,\ldots,r$, of the mapping-space squares for
$$U_k=\prod_{\beta(j)=k}u_j:\prod_{\beta(\alpha(i))=k}e_i\longrightarrow\prod_{\beta(j)=k}e'_j$$
against $z_k$. Its base arrow is the corresponding product of the $f_j$. The regrouping here is the product-cone equivalence. Each $U_k$ is $p$-cocartesian by the product-stability hypothesis, so its square is a homotopy pullback by the definition in the item. If the indexing set is empty, $U_k$ is the identity of $1_{\mathcal E}$ and its square has identity horizontal arrows. Taking a finite product of these squares is again a homotopy pullback: the points and paths specifying a point of a pullback are coordinatewise exactly those of the individual squares. Finally the full mapping spaces are disjoint unions over pointed maps; the lower-left components are indexed by $\beta$, and precomposition sends $\beta$ to $\beta\alpha$. Pulling the lower-right mapping space back to that $\beta$ component therefore selects exactly the square just checked. This proves the full square is a homotopy pullback, even when different $\beta$ have the same $\beta\alpha$. Thus every lift from step 2 is $q$-cocartesian, and $q$ is a cocartesian fibration in the intrinsic convention of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening].

source.place: Theorem 2.1, passage to cocartesian fibrations over the total operad; the cartesian-product mapping-square verification is written out here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] to $q$, using a universe large enough to contain its base and fibers. Obtain the coherent functor $F:\mathcal B^{\times}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. Its value at $(b_i)$ is $\prod_i\mathcal E_{b_i}$. For an inert projection $(b_i)\to b_i$ in $\mathcal B^{\times}$, the block construction in step 2 consists of the identity on $e_i$ and discards the other coordinates, hence its cocartesian transport is the coordinate projection. These identify the arrows $F((b_i))\to F(b_i)$ with the product projections for $n>0$; for $n=0$, step 1 gives $F(())\simeq *$, the required empty product. Pulling $q$ back along the one-coordinate inclusion $\mathcal B\to\mathcal B^{\times}$ gives $p$; naturality of straightening therefore identifies $F|_{\mathcal B}$ with the given $\Phi$, including its transport on arrows.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 2.1, equivalence Fun(C tensor,Cat) with cocartesian fibrations; restriction to one-color fibers.

proof.text: The product-cone condition just verified is exactly the hypothesis of [lem-coef-lax-cartesian-classification], with source $\mathcal B^{\times}$ and target $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$, whose finite products are supplied by [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. It yields a lax symmetric monoidal functor $\mathcal B^{\times}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty^{\times}$. Its restriction at $\langle1\rangle$ is $\Phi$ by step 4. The construction is a functor of total infinity categories over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ preserving inert cocartesian arrows; consequently it supplies every operadic simplex and its face and degeneracy compatibilities. In particular its partition, permutation and nullary compatibilities hold with all their higher homotopies.

source.place: Definition 2.4.1.1 and Proposition 2.4.1.7, as used in Ramzi Theorem 2.1.

proof.text: For a finite set $I$, take the fold arrow $(b_i)_{i\in I}\to(\prod_i b_i)$ in $\mathcal B^{\times}$ represented by the identity of $\prod_i b_i$. Its lift in step 2 is represented by the identity of $\prod_i e_i$. Thus the formula in [lem-coef-lax-cartesian-classification] identifies its structure functor with $(e_i)\mapsto\prod_i e_i$, on objects. For a morphism $(h_i):(e_i)\to(\widetilde e_i)$ in $\prod_i\mathcal E_{b_i}$, the block composition formula identifies both composites around the square between the two identity-block lifts with $\prod_i h_i$. Hence cocartesian transport sends $(h_i)$ to $\prod_i h_i$. The product universal property identifies the corresponding mapping spaces, so the same square argument for parameterized families of morphisms gives the full fiber functor, with all higher simplices. For $I=\varnothing$ it selects $1_{\mathcal E}$ over $1_{\mathcal B}$. Products with their projection cones have contractible choices by their mapping-space universal property; the same is true of the chosen cocartesian lifts, by their displayed mapping-space universal property. The contractible classification choices in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] and [lem-coef-lax-cartesian-classification], together with the functorial cartesian construction of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope], show that this structure is canonical relative to $p$ and its specified classification, as asserted.
